ranking.name: Atlas Tiled Streaming Map Pyramid (architecture #2)
ranking.strengths: Best-balanced of the four: adopts the verified data-model fix verbatim (TSparseArray stable-handle store + uniform hash grid keyed by handle + decoupled Z-index + ~22-28B slim record + per-class ClassDrawTable), which the Stage-1 report names as THE single highest-leverage change that collapses root causes 1+2+leak+O(N^2) load at once. Its render pipeline is the Epic-OFFICIALLY-SANCTIONED TDR fix (UE GPU-crash doc: 'each tile submitted as a separate GPU command buffer'), so bounded per-tile FCanvas EndDraw + scissored HW clear is the PRIMARY path with zero custom shaders — lowest-risk way to make TDR (#14) structurally impossible. Correctly defers the GPU-instanced AbstractInstance/SceneCapture end-state behind validation. Uses in-repo ReliableMessaging (verified int32 SizeType kills the int16 overflow by construction) and fixes #9 by deleting the slice RCO. Server-authoritative per-tile versioned AoI streaming + WP-aligned tiles + IFGSaveInterface persistence make join O(AoI) and chunk-load O(1). VRAM pinned to a fixed ~80-128MB atlas independent of factory size. Its self-identified primary/fallback split exactly matches what the research independently validated.
ranking.weaknesses: Tile-pool/atlas/LRU/page-eviction/mip-pyramid is real systems-engineering surface area — substantially more code than the monolith, with page-eviction thrash and tile-seam (long-belt multi-cell) correctness risks. IFGSaveInterface tile persistence risks save bloat/format churn (derived data that is cheaply recomputable). Headless dedicated-server bake needs a GPU; correctly falls back to client-side baking from server slim lists, but that split adds branching. Slightly heavier than necessary: the persistent render-target tile pyramid is itself a workaround that the Slate-instanced approach (Tessera dossier) shows can be largely avoided.

ranking.name: Cartograph Atlas — Server-Authoritative Tiled Map Streaming (architecture #3)
ranking.strengths: The cleanest, most explicit articulation of the server-authoritative thin-client model — clients never recompute datasets on join or chunk-load, which directly maps onto the Stage-1 finding that the host should iterate AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem as truth and only dedicated-server clients keep a slim store. Same verified data-model core as #2 (TSparseArray slot = stable BuildingId + generation, uniform grid keyed by stable id, separate Z-index/Z-bands, ~28B slim record, per-class ClassDrawTable). Strong, concrete render pipeline: 512^2 atlas pages from a fixed pool with empty tiles costing ZERO VRAM (a genuinely better VRAM story than a fixed monolithic atlas), scissor-clear + MaxPrimitivesPerFrame bounded submission. Shared immutable ref-counted snapshot blobs make join memory O(joiners+AoI) not O(joiners*N) — precisely the Stage-1 'serialize once across joiners' recommendation. Lists the optional AbstractInstance + ortho SceneCapture end-state as gated, correctly.
ranking.weaknesses: Functionally a near-twin of #2; differentiation is mostly framing, so it shares #2's tile-management complexity and headless-bake gap. Embeds tile snapshots in the save via IFGSaveInterface (same recomputable-data/bloat critique). Atlas page-eviction thrash on rapid pan is a named risk. Does not surface the Slate-MakeCustomVerts render primitive that would beat its render-target approach on both VRAM and render-thread cost. The optional GPU-instanced path it cites (USceneCaptureComponent2D + AbstractInstance) needs the unverified GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors isolation on the CSS fork.

ranking.name: Tessera — Stable-Handle Incremental Tile Compositor (architecture #4)
ranking.strengths: Lowest engine-surface and most robust-to-ship of the four, and the ONLY one whose render half the research found a strictly-better primitive for: its dossier shows a custom Slate SLeafWidget emitting FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with a per-instance buffer is ~10x cheaper on the render thread than FCanvas-to-RT (Froyok) AND deletes the persistent VRAM target entirely (64MB -> ~0 persistent), batching all buildings into one instanced draw and removing the global FCanvas hook by construction — the single best render idea across all four dossiers. Data-model half is identical to the verified Stage-1 end-state (TSparseArray + generation, uniform grid, separate Z-band index, 24B FVector3f slim record, per-class FClassDrawInfo, draw-time ComputeDrawGeometry, convergent never-cancel-restarted debounced compositor with a frame-relative budget awaited once-per-tile not per-primitive — directly answering issue #10). Correctly REJECTS the ISM/SceneCapture 'Phase 5 end-state' that Stage-1 floated, with modern evidence that UE5 ISM AddInstance/RemoveInstance regressed badly for high-churn megabases — a sharp, defensible call. Same ReliableMessaging fix for #9.
ranking.weaknesses: Its CHOSEN/stated render path (preserve FCanvas-to-render-target + persistent target + scissored clear + tile pyramid) is the weakest-as-written of the rendering options — the dossier itself flags that Tessera 'doubles down' on the dated canvas pipeline, and the superior MakeCustomVerts idea is the dossier's recommendation TO Tessera, not Tessera's own design. So the architecture as authored under-delivers vs its own research. MakeCustomVerts is not depth-sorted across instances (Z-order must be baked into instance ordering) and is a UMG/Slate-shaped tool that re-expresses the mip-pyramid as instance-count culling — extra rework. Its minimal-engine-surface philosophy also forgoes the GPU-driven ceiling the others reach for if a megabase still hitches.

ranking.name: Cartograph Atlas: server-authoritative ECS column store + GPU-driven tiled compute rasterizer (architecture #1)
ranking.strengths: Highest theoretical optimization ceiling and the most rigorous data model: an SoA/ECS column store keyed by FBuildingHandle{slot,gen} with per-CLASS draw table, uniform fixed-cell grid, coarse Z-band index, and a persistent GPU instance StructuredBuffer — the purest expression of 'one source of truth, stable handles, cost bounded by viewport+frame, O(1) mutation' that the Stage-1 report demands. Its killer-feature framing (cost bounded by VIEWPORT and FRAME, not factory size; per-event collapses to 'patch one slot + set a dirty bit') is exactly correct and the strongest articulation of the end-state goal. GPU-driven instanced/indirect rendering into per-tile scissored passes with a hard per-frame primitive ceiling is the tightest possible VRAM/bandwidth/TDR control. Network/server/memory designs are first-rate and match the others. Honestly self-identifies the RDG-from-a-mod risk and ships an FCanvas-per-tile fallback.
ranking.weaknesses: Its PRIMARY render path — a hand-rolled RDG compute/indirect-draw rasterizer with custom global shaders — is the single highest feasibility risk on the CSS fork: it needs a separate PostConfigInit shader module or the ShaderDirectoryMapper trick (the Cartograph GameFeature is LoadingPhase=Default with no Shaders dir), wrestles renderer-private headers, and must validate shader cooking in SML shipping/dedicated-server configs. The research is unanimous that this is the WRONG path to take first and that stock SceneCapture orthographic-tiling + AbstractInstance reach the same TDR/VRAM guarantees with zero custom shaders. So the architecture as-authored front-loads its own #1 keyRisk. Also over-engineers vs in-repo reality: it proposes hand-building a TSparseArray instance buffer + manual StructuredBuffer patching when AbstractInstance already provides stable handles, O(1) add/remove with swap-patch, per-class bucketing, and per-instance custom data — verified present in Plugins/AbstractInstance. Highest total complexity for a marginal ceiling gain over the bounded-submission approaches.

bestOfBreed.dataModel: WINNER: architecture #1 (Atlas ECS column store), with identity/handle mechanics from #4/#3. WHY: all four converge on the verified Stage-1 fix (stable generational handle as identity; uniform hash grid keyed by that handle; SEPARATE Z-band index decoupled from storage so the operator<=> Z-sort coupling that forced renumbering is deleted; ~24-28B slim record; per-CLASS draw table of hundreds of entries; engine-as-truth on host so no second factory copy). #1 is best because it goes furthest: a true SoA/ECS COLUMN store (column Pos FVector3f, column Yaw packed, column ClassId u16, column Type, column ExtraIndex) is the most cache-friendly layout for the per-dirty-cell gather and the GPU instance-buffer patch, drops FTransform quat+scale entirely (top-down needs only yaw), and stores NOTHING that is a pure function of transform+class. CRITICAL REPO-VERIFIED REFINEMENT: do NOT hand-build the instance buffer — back the store with AbstractInstance (Plugins/AbstractInstance, currently commented out at Cartograph.Build.cs:49; FInstanceOwnerHandlePtr is the stable handle, SetInstanceFromDataStatic/RemoveInstance are O(1) with internal swap-patch, SetCustomPrimitiveDataOnHandle carries worldZ/layerId/colorIndex via NumCustomDataFloats). Engine is UE 5.6.1-CSS (verified in FactoryGame.uproject), so current AbstractInstance custom-data + GPU Scene auto-instancing are fully available. Its handle is TSharedPtr<...,NotThreadSafe> = game-thread only, and it builds collision by default (ULightweightCollisionComponent) — disable collision for a visual-only marker layer.
bestOfBreed.renderPipeline: PRIMARY WINNER: architecture #4's render PRIMITIVE as corrected by its own research — a custom Slate SLeafWidget emitting FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts with a per-instance buffer — because it is ~10x cheaper on the render thread than FCanvas-to-RT (Froyok), batches all buildings into ONE instanced draw, deletes the persistent VRAM render target (64-256MB -> ~0 persistent), and removes the global FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook (a process-wide tax + cross-mod static_cast hazard flagged in Stage-1) by construction. Pair it with #2/#3's BOUNDED-SUBMISSION discipline and #1's per-frame PRIMITIVE CEILING + monotonic dirty-tile draining so a megabase first-paint still drains across frames under the ~2s TDR. SECOND/SAFE-PRIMARY: the bounded per-tile FCanvas EndDraw + scissored HW ClearRenderTargetView of #2/#3 — the Epic-OFFICIALLY-SANCTIONED TDR pattern (UE GPU-crash doc: each tile = separate command buffer), needs zero custom shaders, and should ship FIRST as the de-risking bridge. END-STATE (gated, not first): GPU-instanced AbstractInstance + orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D with NATIVE bEnableOrthographicTiling (available on 5.6) that #1/#2/#3 cite — but ONLY after validating GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors capture isolation on the CSS fork. REJECT as primary: #1's hand-rolled RDG compute/indirect rasterizer (highest feasibility risk; demote to profiled optional Phase-N). NOTE the Stage-1 'Phase 5 ISM end-state' should be treated cautiously per #4's evidence of UE5 ISM high-churn regressions — mitigate with collision disabled + MarkDirtyDeferred batching, keep the bounded canvas/Slate path as the safe fallback.
bestOfBreed.asyncThreading: WINNER: shared across all four (identical here), articulated most cleanly by #1 and #4. WHY: replace the cancel-restart-on-every-event coroutine (Stage-1 amplifier root cause 4) with a SINGLE long-lived convergent compositor that is NEVER cancelled and a MONOTONIC dirty-tile/dirty-rect set that only ever grows then drains — build hooks do O(1) work (patch handle + set dirty bits) and enqueue nothing heavy, so a belt-drag converges continuously instead of thrashing to zero completed frames. Keep the existing UE5Coro FTickTimeBudget model (frame-RELATIVE fraction of frame time, the correct answer to issue #10) but await ONCE per tile / per K buildings, NOT per primitive (kills the ~9*N awaiter + FPlatformTime::Cycles() reads Stage-1 flagged). Off the game thread via UE::Tasks::Launch (5.6 native): per-dirty-cell POD snapshot packing and network-delta/tile-blob serialization on workers; only the small mapped-buffer/instance-handle writes and the debounced capture/flush on the game thread (AbstractInstance handles are NotThreadSafe/game-thread-only — honor that). Backpressure: coalesce a tile dirtied 100x into one render, prioritize the player's current map-viewport AoI first.
bestOfBreed.networkTransport: WINNER: shared by all four, on the in-repo ReliableMessaging plugin (Plugins/ReliableMessaging) — REPO-VERIFIED: SizeType = TArray<uint8>::SizeType (int32), so the int16 slice-overflow bug class is gone by construction; transports include TCP (links on dedicated server) + EOSP2P + SteamP2P. WHY: delete the hand-rolled slice RCO wholesale (the source of #9: three unchecked TMap::Find null-derefs racing the 10s timeout, int16 overflow at ~63MB, move-unsafe FBufferWriter, per-join synchronous full Archive<<CurrentBuildingData) and replace with SendTaggedMessage(PC, FGameplayTag, payload) over its chunked/acked/windowed/backpressured uint64-id transport keyed to a per-PlayerController component with disconnect teardown. The design is DELTA-BY-TILE-VERSION / per-AoI lazy pull, NOT reliable-multicast-per-event (#1/#2/#3 all specify this): server bumps a per-tile content version (= hash of authoritative content, not a session counter, for deterministic reconnect), coalesces per net-tick, streams only changed AoI tiles. CRITICAL VERIFIED CAVEAT (confirmed in ReliableMessagingPlayerComponent.h): SendTaggedMessage takes the payload BY VALUE and the send queue is strict FIFO — keep blobs PER-TILE/slim, use a small FIXED gameplay-tag set (manifest/tile/version, not a tag-per-tile), add app-level AoI ordering, init the transport + handshake at world load, and hold one shared TSharedRef snapshot pinned across joiners (join memory O(N), not O(joiners*N)).
bestOfBreed.serverClientPartitioning: WINNER: architecture #3 (server-authoritative thin client), the cleanest formulation, reinforced by #1's host engine-as-truth split. WHY: exactly matches the Stage-1 directive — the HOST/listen-server reads AFGBuildableSubsystem/AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem as the single source of truth and keeps ZERO second copy (only grid + Z-index + per-class table + the render-side instance buffer), so single-player/listen pays zero serialization and zero duplication; the DEDICATED SERVER holds the authoritative indices + per-tile slim blobs but renders NOTHING (no atlas/VRAM/render-thread cost); only DEDICATED-SERVER CLIENTS (which lack subsystem data) keep the slim SoA store, and only for their AoI tiles. Align tiles to World Partition cell granularity so chunk-load is an O(1) version check, never a recompute — but DESIGN-AROUND CONSTRAINT: World Partition is not moddable, lightweight indices can be renumbered by the engine, and not all regions are resident, so use generation-guarded {class,index} keys and reconcile-on-load; do NOT conflate the map-UI viewport AoI with the player's world-streaming AoI. Persist derived state ONLY as an optional recomputable cache (treat the save as a cache reconciled in PostLoadGame), not as a correctness dependency — lighter than #2/#3's default IFGSaveInterface tile embedding.
bestOfBreed.memoryModel: WINNER: architecture #1 (most rigorous accounting), tied with #4 for the host/client split. WHY: the end-state every design targets — DELETE the ~344-432B FBuildingData second copy and its ~152-192B precomputed draw caches (recomputed on draw from a per-class table), DELETE the never-compacting IndexRedirector (the session-long O(cumulative-adds) leak), DELETE the TQuadTree 40B/element FBox2D (replaced by the grid). #1 quantifies it best: host CPU-RAM ~8-12B/building of indices (vs ~430MB-equiv today) because geometry is read live from the engine and consumed transiently per dirty cell; dedicated-server client ~28B/building slim SoA for AoI tiles only; VRAM a FIXED CEILING set by the atlas (~84MB) INDEPENDENT of building count — 200k, 1M, or 50M all cost the same because the image is viewport-sized not factory-sized. The instance StructuredBuffer (~16B/building) is the only count-scaling GPU buffer and can be paged per-AoI. #4 improves the VRAM line further if the Slate-MakeCustomVerts renderer is adopted: persistent render-target VRAM drops from 64MB toward ~0 (the on-screen panel composites via Slate's own swap-chain pass). Generational handles add ~4B/slot. Net: peak RAM and VRAM both decoupled from runaway growth, FLAT across a build/dismantle session — the explicit #14 success criterion.

synthesisGuidance:
Build ONE system: the four proposals are ~85% the same architecture independently rediscovered; treat them as a single design with four render-pipeline variants and merge the strongest piece of each. The non-render layers are already in agreement and should be taken as the shared spine.

SHARED SPINE (adopt verbatim, all four agree; this is the verified Stage-1 end-state): (1) Identity = stable generational handle, NEVER a positional index. Storage = SoA/ECS column store (#1) keyed by that handle. Spatial index = uniform hash grid over the constexpr world bounds (WEST/EAST/NORTH/SOUTH verified present) keyed by the handle. Z-filter = a SEPARATE coarse Z-band index, decoupled from storage. Slim ~24-28B record; per-CLASS draw table; all screen geometry recomputed at draw via one shared pure ComputeDrawGeometry helper. This single change collapses root causes 1+2+leak+O(N^2) load simultaneously and is the mandatory first ship. (2) Async = one never-cancelled convergent compositor draining a monotonic dirty set under a frame-RELATIVE UE5Coro budget awaited per-tile, with UE::Tasks workers for POD packing. (3) Network = delete the slice RCO, use ReliableMessaging SendTaggedMessage with delta-by-tile-version per-AoI pull (mind the by-value payload + FIFO + fixed-tag-set caveats). (4) Partition = host/listen reads engine subsystems as truth (zero second copy); dedicated server holds indices + slim blobs and renders nothing; dedicated clients hold slim AoI store only.

RENDER = the one real divergence; sequence it to de-risk, do NOT pick one variant outright: Phase A ship the SHARED SPINE on the EXISTING canvas with #2/#3's bounded per-tile EndDraw + scissored HW clear + persistent target (Epic-sanctioned, zero custom shaders) — this alone kills #14 TDR and the VRAM monolith at lowest risk. Phase B evaluate #4's Slate FSlateDrawElement::MakeCustomVerts instanced widget as the render primitive: it is ~10x cheaper and deletes the persistent VRAM target, the single best render idea in the dossiers, and should become the default 2D path if its Z-ordering (bake draw order into instance order via the Z-band index) and zoom-LOD (instance-count culling replacing texture mips) prove out. Phase C (gated end-state) the GPU-instanced AbstractInstance marker layer + orthographic USceneCaptureComponent2D with native bEnableOrthographicTiling — adopt ONLY after validating GetViewOwner/ShowOnlyActors capture isolation on the CSS fork. REJECT architecture #1's hand-rolled RDG/custom-shader rasterizer as the primary path; keep it as a profiled optional Phase-N only.

CONFLICTS TO RESOLVE: (1) ENGINE VERSION: the prompt says UE 5.3.2 but FactoryGame.uproject is verified 5.6.1-CSS. This is decisive and in the design's favor — it removes nearly all 'needs-newer-ue' gates (native ortho tiling, current AbstractInstance custom-data, UE::Tasks, GPU Scene auto-instancing are all available). Re-tag every technique against 5.6.1, not 5.3. (2) RENDER PRIMITIVE conflict: #2/#3 keep a render-target tile pyramid; #4 (via its research) shows Slate-instanced geometry makes the persistent target and most tile machinery unnecessary. Resolve by KEEPING the tile/dirty-rect CONCEPT for CPU-side culling + budgeted convergence + per-tile network versioning, but making the IMAGE Slate-instanced geometry rather than a composited render target where feasible. (3) ISM/SceneCapture end-state conflict: Stage-1 and #1/#2/#3 treat it as the desirable GPU end-state; #4 argues UE5 ISM AddInstance/RemoveInstance regressed for high-churn megabases. Resolve empirically — gate it, disable collision (AbstractInstance builds it by default, verified), batch via MarkDirtyDeferred, and never make it the only renderer; the bounded canvas/Slate path stays as the always-available fallback. (4) PERSISTENCE conflict: #2/#3 embed tile snapshots in the save via IFGSaveInterface; #1/#4 treat derived state as a recomputable runtime cache. Resolve toward recomputable-cache (version = content hash, reconcile in PostLoadGame) to avoid save bloat/format churn; make any save-embedding optional and content-hash-validated. (5) HANDLE-vs-INSTANCE-BUFFER conflict: #1 hand-builds a TSparseArray instance buffer + manual StructuredBuffer patching; the repo already ships AbstractInstance (commented out at Build.cs:49) providing stable handles + O(1) swap-patch + per-class bucketing + custom data. Resolve by adopting AbstractInstance as the handle/instance store and reserving a hand-rolled buffer only if AbstractInstance's game-thread-only NotThreadSafe handles or default collision prove blocking."
